Conflict of Interest Policy: The document defining conflicts of interest, disclosure obligations, and recusal processes. [Ch. 34]
Consequence Management: The consistent application of appropriate consequences for conduct violations. [Ch. 35]
CPD (Continuing Professional Development): The systematic maintenance of professional knowledge and skills throughout a career. [Ch. 35]
Delegation of Authority (DoA): The document mapping financial and operational approval authority from Board to individual managers. [Ch. 34]
EVP (Employee Value Proposition): The total package of benefits and experiences offered to employees to attract and retain them. [Ch. 35]
Executive Committee (ExCo): The primary management decision-making forum chaired by the MD/CEO. [Ch. 34]
Fit and Proper Standard: NAICOM’s requirements for directors and key management personnel. [Ch. 34]
Independent Director: A non-executive director with no material relationship to the company, its shareholders, or management. [Ch. 34]
Internal Audit: The independent assurance function providing the Board with objective assessment of controls and risk management; the third line of defence. [Ch. 34]
Investment Committee: The Board committee responsible for overseeing the Investment Policy Statement and investment portfolio performance. [Ch. 34]
KPI (Key Performance Indicator): A specific, measurable metric for evaluating performance against targets. [Ch. 35]
MD/CEO (Managing Director / Chief Executive Officer): The most senior executive of the company, accountable to the Board for overall management. [Ch. 34]
Non-Executive Director (NED): A Board member without an executive management role; provides independent oversight. [Ch. 34]

OKRs (Objectives and Key Results): A goal-setting framework using ambitious qualitative objectives and specific measurable results; a quarterly execution complement to the Balanced Scorecard. [Ch. 27]
Remuneration Committee: The Board committee setting remuneration policy for the Board and senior management. [Ch. 34]
Risk Committee: The Board committee overseeing the ERM framework, risk appetite, and ORSA. [Ch. 34]
Span of Control: The number of direct reports managed by a single manager. [Ch. 34]
Succession Planning: The systematic identification and development of candidates for critical roles. [Ch. 35]
Three Lines of Defence: See Entry in Section 10.
Tone from the Top: The principle that senior leadership behaviour is the most powerful determinant of organisational culture. [Ch. 35]
Terms specific to the Nigerian insurance market, institutions, and cultural context.
Africa Re (African Reinsurance Corporation): The pan-African reinsurer owned by African Union member states; a major domestic reinsurance capacity provider for Nigerian cedants. [Ch. 14]

Ajo: A Yoruba term for a traditional rotating savings and credit association (ROSCA); a community-based informal savings mechanism that competes with insurance as a financial protection tool. [Ch. 22]
CBN (Central Bank of Nigeria): The apex bank regulator; relevant to insurance for bancassurance regulatory coordination and financial system stability. [Ch. 16]
CIIN (Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria): The professional body for insurance practitioners in Nigeria, conducting examinations, awarding qualifications, and setting CPD standards. [Ch. 35]
Continental Reinsurance (Continental Re): A major pan-African reinsurer headquartered in Lagos. [Ch. 14]

Cooperative Society: A member-owned organisation providing savings, credit, and mutual support; a major community distribution channel for microinsurance and informal sector financial services. [Ch. 22]
CIIN Cert. COP: The CIIN Certificate of Proficiency; the minimum licensing qualification for insurance agents under NIIRA 2025. [Ch. 35]
Domestic Cession: The regulatory requirement for Nigerian insurers to offer a defined proportion of their reinsurance to Nigerian domestic reinsurers before placing internationally. [Ch. 14]
EFInA: Enhancing Financial Innovation and Access; the primary source of demand-side data on financial inclusion and insurance in Nigeria. [Ch. 36]
EFU Life Tables: The Experience Follows Up (EFU) Nigerian life mortality tables; NAICOM’s recommended mortality tables for life insurance pricing. [Ch. 13]
Esusu: An Igbo term for a traditional rotating savings and credit association; equivalent to Ajo. [Ch. 22]
Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN): The issuer of FGN bonds and Sukuk, the primary fixed-income admissible assets for Nigerian insurers. [Ch. 23]
FIRS (Federal Inland Revenue Service): The federal tax authority; governs the tax treatment of insurance premiums and benefits under PITA. [Ch. 25]
FMDQ: Financial Markets Dealers Quotations; the securities exchange where FGN bonds, commercial paper, and other fixed-income instruments are listed and traded. [Ch. 23]
Gross Domestic Product (GDP): The total value of goods and services produced in Nigeria in a year; insurance penetration is typically expressed as a percentage of GDP. [Ch. 21]
IAN (Institute of Actuaries of Nigeria): The Nigerian actuarial professional body. [Ch. 13]
Jaiz Bank: Nigeria’s first fully fledged Islamic bank; a potential Takaful distribution partner. [Ch. 29]
Mandatory Insurance: Insurance required by law, including the mandatory group life obligation under the PRA 2014, mandatory credit life under NIIRA 2025, and TPMI for motor vehicles. [Ch. 21]
NAFDAC: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control; relevant to health insurance in certifying drugs covered under HMO formularies. [Ch. 32]
NBS (National Bureau of Statistics): The government statistical agency; a key source of household income, expenditure, and demographic data for insurance market research. [Ch. 36]
NGX (Nigerian Exchange Group): The Nigerian Stock Exchange and its affiliated markets; the primary equity market for Shari’ah-screened investments and listed insurer securities. [Ch. 23]
NIA (Nigerian Insurers Association): The trade association for licensed Nigerian insurers; a collective voice for the industry with NAICOM and the public. [Ch. 36]
NIIRA 2025: See entry in Section 8. [Ch. 21]
NIN (National Identification Number): The unique identifier issued by NIMC; required for insurance KYC and policy issuance. [Ch. 21]
NIMC (National Identity Management Commission): The federal agency managing the national identity system; NIN verification is a key KYC tool for Nigerian insurers. [Ch. 21]
NRC (Nigerian Reinsurance Corporation): A government-linked domestic reinsurer. [Ch. 14]
Pari Passu: On equal footing; relevant in the context of co-insurance where all participating insurers share claims in proportion to their participation. [Ch. 14]
PenCom: National Pension Commission; see Section 15. [Ch. 33]
PITA (Personal Income Tax Act): The primary Nigerian income tax legislation; governs the tax treatment of insurance premiums and retirement savings. [Ch. 25]
Premium Tax: A tax on insurance premiums levied in some jurisdictions; the specific Nigerian treatment is governed by FIRS guidance. [Ch. 21]
Third Party Motor Insurance (TPMI): The minimum mandatory motor insurance under the Motor Vehicles (Third Party Insurance) Act. [Ch. 21]

blocks.title: Section 18: CIIN Examination and Professional Development Terms

blocks.h: Qualification frameworks, examination terminology, and study guidance.
ACIIN (Associate of the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria): The Associateship qualification; a higher professional designation required for key management roles under NIIRA 2025. [Ch. 35]
Analyse: An examination command word requiring the candidate to break a concept or situation into its components and examine each in detail.
Assess: An examination command word requiring the candidate to evaluate the value, importance, or implications of a topic.
Case Study Question: An examination question presenting a real or hypothetical business scenario, requiring application of knowledge to the specific facts given.
CIIN Annual Conference: The Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria’s flagship professional development event; generates CPD credit hours. [Ch. 35]
CIIN Examination Diet: A scheduled sitting of CIIN examinations; typically held at least twice per year. [Ch. 35]
CIIN Examination Levels: Three levels: Foundation (Certificate of Proficiency and Cert. CIIN); Diploma (Dip. CIIN); Associateship (ACIIN) and Fellowship (FCIIN). [Ch. 35]
Compare and Contrast: An examination command word requiring identification of similarities and differences between two or more items.
CPD (Continuing Professional Development): The ongoing maintenance of professional knowledge; CIIN members must complete defined hours annually. [Ch. 35]
Critically Evaluate: An examination command word at Associateship level requiring a balanced, evidence-based assessment of a proposition, including arguments for and against.
Define: An examination command word requiring a precise, concise statement of the meaning of a term.
Describe: An examination command word requiring a detailed account of a concept, process, or product.
Dip. CIIN (Diploma in Insurance): The intermediate CIIN qualification, covering underwriting, claims, reinsurance, distribution, and risk management. [Ch. 35]
Discuss: An examination command word requiring a balanced consideration of multiple aspects of a topic.
Distinguish: An examination command word requiring identification of the differences between two or more terms or concepts.
Essay Question: A long-form examination question requiring a structured, discursive response at Associateship level.
Evaluate: See Critically Evaluate.
Explain: An examination command word requiring a clear, logical account of how or why something works or happens.
FCIIN (Fellow of the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria): The Fellowship qualification; the highest CIIN designation, typically held by senior practitioners and leaders. [Ch. 35]
Identify: An examination command word requiring a list or specific naming of items without extended explanation.
IFoA (Institute and Faculty of Actuaries): The UK professional body for actuaries; many Nigerian actuaries qualify through the IFoA. [Ch. 13]
Illustrate: An examination command word requiring demonstration of a concept through examples or worked calculations.
MCQ (Multiple Choice Question): A Foundation and Diploma examination question format presenting four options, one of which is correct. [Ch. 38]
Model Answer: The examiner’s indicative ideal answer, typically providing more information than the maximum mark-earning response. [Ch. 38]
Module: A defined unit of study within a CIIN qualification, assessed by a single examination paper.
Outline: An examination command word requiring a structured summary without full detail; less depth than ‘describe’.
Professional Indemnity Insurance: Insurance protecting professionals against claims of negligent advice or service; relevant to financial advisers and insurance practitioners. [Ch. 18]
Recommend: An examination command word requiring the candidate to make and justify a specific course of action based on the facts of the question.
Structured CPD: Formal, documented learning activities that generate CIIN CPD credit hours. [Ch. 35]
Study Leave: Employer-granted time for examination preparation; best practice for insurers sponsoring CIIN qualifications. [Ch. 35]
Syllabus Mapping: The alignment of textbook content to CIIN examination syllabus topics; this glossary chapter provides a reference index for examination preparation. [Ch. 38]
